segments.name: High-performance computing
segments.note: Chips for AI data centers and high-performance computing — the AI build-out, and now more than two-thirds of everything TSMC sells.

segments.name: Smartphone
segments.note: Chips for phones — still the second-biggest business, but down to about a fifth of revenue as AI takes over.

segments.name: Internet of Things
segments.note: Chips for connected devices, from wearables to industrial sensors.

segments.name: Automotive
segments.note: Chips for cars — the fastest-growing platform this quarter, up 23% from Q2.

segments.name: Digital consumer electronics
segments.note: Chips for TVs, game consoles and other consumer gadgets — the smallest slice.

segments.name: Others
segments.note: Everything else TSMC makes that doesn't fit the big five platforms.

opex.name: Operating expenses
opex.note: Research, engineering and running the fabs' business side — TSMC reports this as one line in its earnings release.

oneTimers: Non-operating income fell to NT$34.6B from NT$95.8B in Q2 2026, when TSMC booked unusually large non-operating gains — that is why net income grew only 8% from Q2 while operating income grew 14%.
verdict: TSMC's revenue leapt 51% to a record US$46.7B as AI demand made high-performance computing 68% of sales — and with a 66% gross margin, it kept about 51 cents of every dollar as profit.
otherDetail: Non-operating income of NT$34.6B (about $1.1B) — mostly interest earned on TSMC's large cash pile.
footerNote: TSMC reports in New Taiwan dollars (revenue NT$1,494.2B; net income NT$763.1B). Dollar figures are converted at the quarter's average rate of NT$31.98 per US$1 — the rate TSMC itself reports; its stated US-dollar revenue was $46.72B. Operating expenses are shown as one line, net of about NT$0.5B of other operating income, because the earnings release does not split them out.

takeaways.title: AI chips are the business
takeaways.text: High-performance computing — mostly AI accelerators — was 68% of revenue and grew 22% from Q2. Advanced chips (7nm and below) were 79% of wafer revenue, and the newest 2nm node already contributed 8%.

takeaways.title: Margins most companies dream of
takeaways.text: Gross margin of 66.4%, operating margin of 58.7% and a net margin of 51.1% — TSMC keeps more than half of every sales dollar as profit, even while spending heavily on new fabs.

takeaways.title: Next quarter guided higher still
takeaways.text: Management guided Q4 2026 revenue to US$52.3–54.3B, driven by the steep ramp of 2nm production — the quarter ahead is expected to be bigger than this record one.

follow100Note: Kept-as-profit includes +$2.32 of other income per $100 of revenue; the rows add to $99.99 due to rounding.
